To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of keywords in a document can be used as an indication of the quality of the writing, that the use of a keyword in a document can predict the use of that keyword in other documents, and that the use of words in a document is correlated with the use of other words in that document.

(1) automatic extraction of keywords from documents is a difficult task, (2) automatic keyword extraction from individual texts is possible with a high level of accuracy (up to 80% in the best cases), and (3) automatic extraction of a set of keywords that are common to a collection of documents is possible with a lower level of accuracy than the previous case, but still acceptable (up to 70% in the best case)

1) the most important keywords in a document are not the most frequent words in the document; 2) the most important words in a document tend to be longer than the most frequent words; 3) the most important keyword phrases in a document tend not to be the longest phrases; and 4) the most important phrases in a document are longer than the most common phrases.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to obtain the most informative keywords, we need to take into account not only the document’s content but also its context, that is the context in which it is used.
, while keyword extraction from individual articles is a challenging problem, the task becomes much easier when the articles are grouped into clusters.
, in general, the best keywords for a document are not necessarily the most frequent ones.
